text:
maya: heads up — trying to get the new JS SDK running in an edge runtime (Vercel Edge Functions) and hit a weird error when importing. works in node but fails at runtime with 'Cannot use import statement outside a module'.

maya: minimal repro: import { Redwood } from 'redwood-sdk' in an edge lambda. bundler is esbuild via next.

maya: package.json exports currently look like: 
```json
{
  "main": "dist/cjs/index.js",
  "module": "dist/esm/index.js",
  "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
      "import": "./dist/esm/index.js"
    }
  }
}
```

maya: edge runtime seems to pick the cjs path and then crash. any quick wins?

tony: could be a resolver/bundler issue. next's edge build sometimes rewrites to the cjs entry if imports are ambiguous. are you using "type": "module" in package.json?

maya: not currently. we made dual builds to support old consumers.

sarah: fwiw we ran into similar with the auth helper earlier — some bundles ended up bundling node-only retry logic and broke on edge. suggestion: ship an explicit entry for the edge target and a lighter runtime-only client.

ryan: +1. Another option is to add an explicit conditional export for the edge/runtime environment like: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  }
}
```

ryan: then consumers that support the "edge" condition (some bundlers) pick the small ESM build. fallback remains.

tony: also check types entrypoint — we should expose types via the "types" field and also add an exports condition for "types" to avoid tsc resolution weirdness in monorepos. otherwise editors can resolve to wrong declaration and suggest CJS runtime types.

maya: good point. currently types point to dist/index.d.ts only. want to avoid nested path resolution issues.

sarah: on auth/retry — we found retry middleware pulled in global fetch polyfills which made edge builds bundle a ton. splitting auth into a thin transport-agnostic interface + adapters per environment helped. then edge adapter uses native fetch; node adapter uses node-fetch or undici and retry logic.

maya: that seems like a bigger refactor but probably best for parity. can we patch a temporary fix? maybe publish a small ESM-only package like @redwood/sdk-edge with minimal surface for a few weeks?

tony: we can publish a scoped shim. downside: it splinters packages and docs, onboarding friction increases. but pragmatic short-term.

ryan: alternative quick fix — set "exports" default import to the esm path and set "main" to cjs. many bundlers prefer exports/import mapping over main. but risky for older require-only consumers.

devex-bot: reminder — if we change exports, update the SDK migration guide and changelog so integrators know about conditional exports.

maya: +1. I'll open a PR with two patches: 1) conditional exports with an "edge" condition that points to a tiny ESM build, 2) add a "types" condition mapping.

ci-bot: build pipeline report: CI will need matrix changes — add esbuild target run against the dist/edge build and a types-only validation to catch missing declarations.

sarah: happy to review the PR — also let's add a simple smoke sample in examples/next-edge that imports exactly like the user would. helps catch bundler rewrites.

maya: thanks all. creating PR now and will link the sample app in the PR description.

tony: when you open the PR, ping me. I can run quick compatibility tests against our internal monorepos to catch any require-only consumers.

maya: will do. :thumbsup:
